report.summary: The change replaces the owner-only check requireProject(ctx.env, ctx.user.id, projectId) with requireReadableProject, which also accepts any project whose visibility is "public". All issue, comment and label handlers go through withOwnedRepository, so any signed-in non-owner can now read, create, update and delete issues, comments and labels on another user's public Artifacts project. This contradicts docs/11 P3 (issues stay owner-only for every project) and docs/09 (functions require an owned Artifacts project). No spec change goes with it, and no test refuses visitors as tab 11 requires.

findings.text: Issue, comment and label handlers now authorize non-owners on public projects, including mutations (create/update/delete issues, comments, labels). Spec requires owner-only access for every project.

evidence.quote: const project = await requireReadableProject(ctx.env, ctx.user, projectId);
evidence.why: requireReadableProject in common.ts only throws when `!row || (row.userId !== viewer?.id && row.visibility !== "public")`, so for a public project owned by user A, signed-in user B passes and reaches createArtifactIssue/updateArtifactIssue/deleteArtifactIssue/deleteArtifactLabel etc. docs/11 Public Profile.md P3: "Issues, pull requests, checks, conversations and workspaces stay owner-only for every project." docs/09 Git Forge.md: "All issue, comment and label functions use the existing owner authentication and require an owned Artifacts project." The previous requireProject filtered on eq(schema.projects.userId, userId).

findings.text: Behavior changes without a spec update in docs/09, docs/11 or IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES (CLAUDE.md rule 16). The tab 11 required test 'visitors refused for issues … of a public project' is not present, so nothing catches this regression.

evidence.why: The only file changed is issues.ts. No docs or tests change, and a search of apps/tempo test files found no public-visibility issue test.

checked.risk: Security: ownership and visibility checks on issue/comment/label handlers
Spec conformance for issue access on public projects
Failure paths: error masking in withOwnedRepository is unchanged (TempoError rethrown, others become INTERNAL)
Tests: whether coverage exists for visitor refusal on public-project issues
Real contracts, idempotency, build environment: not affected; the change only swaps the authorization helper
